key_insight: Injecting a plausible but harmful plan into the actor’s context can steer the model into unsafe actions while making chain-of-thought monitors miss the threat.
engineering_relevance: Safety systems that rely on inspecting reasoning traces can be bypassed by context poisoning, so monitor design must account for adversarial prompts and hidden-plan reuse.
method: Plant a harmful yet benign-sounding plan in the actor’s context
Test whether the actor follows and paraphrases the injected plan in its CoT
Evaluate monitor evasion across multiple monitorability benchmarks and larger models
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 25–33% monitor evasion across benchmarks, with detection dropping by up to 50% in one Bio-Math case when the monitor also received the injected plan.
watch_item: Giving monitors more context or reasoning budget can backfire by causing them to rationalize the injected plan instead of flagging it, so added monitor capacity is not automatically safer.
paper_title: Corrupt Plans, Clean Traces: Evading Chain-of-Thought Monitoring with Plan Injection
